FN-80J92F-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 16
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Representative Chris England
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 03/17/2023
House Bill 16as introduced creates the eight-member Criminal Justice Policy Development
Council to 1) update the inmate classification system; 2) create parole guidelines; 3) adopt a
validated risk and needs assessment for felony offenders; and 4) provide quarterly reports to the
Legislature beginning on October 1, 2023. This bill could increase the obligations of the various
assisting agencies by an undetermined amount dependent on the cost of 1) third party contracts
entered into by the council to assist in the development of these policies, as provided by this bill;
and 2) expenses incurred by council members for attending meeting of the council. This bill
could also increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Corrections and the
Board of Pardons and Paroles to implement the systems, guidelines, and policies adopted by the
council.
In addition, this bill could further increase or decrease the administrative obligations of the
board to 1) use parole release guidelines in parole decisions; 2) provide an explanation when
deviating from these guidelines; and 3) provide written notification to the prisoner of their right
to appeal a parole denial by the board that deviated from these guidelines to the Court of
Criminal Appeals, as provided by this bill.
